Iran this week unveiled a huge billboard and banners over Enqelab Square in central Tehran. The billboard pledged in English: “We will kill Trump” – elevating the degree of personal animus with which Donald Trump is viewed in official Iranian circles.

The poster depicts the US president behind bars with his head bowed. Passing through the Mojave desert on State Route 14, going by landscapes Hollywood uses to represent alien planets, a driver might not expect to find a walkable, tree-lined boulevard.

But there are nine beautiful, leafy blocks on West Lancaster Boulevard, a piece of what used to be Highway 14. They were redeveloped as part of a mixed-use urban streetscape in the city of Lancaster, California in 2010.

The BLVD, as it’s been rebranded, is home to 250 public and private enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums, a performing arts centre and a public library. City Hall is just a block south.

The city invested $11.5m (£8.5m) to transform a busy thoroughfare into an inviting public space. The three lanes in the centre of the former five-lane road were replaced by a series of tree-lined ramblas – Spanish for “avenue” and “watercourse,” because dry stream beds served as streets in early cities.

The redesign was planned and funded by the city of redevelopment agency. Within four years of completion, it had generated more than $270m in economic output, attracted $130m in investment, created hundreds of jobs and prompted the building or renovation of hundreds of housing units, according to the city.

The revitalisation has also created more intangible benefits, residents say.. The city centre the feels like a gathering space, they said — somewhere where they can feel like part of a community.

events.title: 'Identity crisis': Can Democrats 'deliver' following their 'historic', once in a generation victory?
events.summary: A historic Democratic electoral breakthrough has transformed the American political landscape, but the magnitude of the victory may intensify competing claims over the party's future direction. For former US diplomat and political analyst Laurie Dunden, the central question is whether the Democratic Party can convert electoral momentum into coherent governance. "Can they deliver?" she asks, capturing the fundamental tension between electoral success and political effectiveness. Dunden examines the apparent disintegration of Donald Trump's 2024 electoral coalition alongside the Democratic Party's continuing ideological struggle between its progressive and centrist wings ahead of the 2028 presidential election. All the while, Dunden cautions against prematurely describing Trump as a lame duck: "Trump is never going to stop being Trump." The resulting struggle over congressional spending powers, presidential vetoes, tariffs and investigations promises to test the practical boundaries of American checks and balances. "This dance is going to be very delicate to watch."

events.summary: Parties led by Israel’s Arab minority made historic gains, winning a combined 19 seats in a race in which Palestinians with Israeli citizenship headed to the polls in record numbers.
